q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text: Yes, ibuprofen (Motrin) can be given to a child over 6 months old, according to MedlinePlus [6]. It helps reduce fever, and is usually given every 6 to 8 hours [6]. Do not give it to a child who is dehydrated, has chickenpox, or has asthma unless a doctor recommends it, according to the NHS [3]. Check the packaging or leaflet to make sure the medicine suits your child, or ask a pharmacist if you are unsure [4].

q: my son threw up twice this morning, what should I give him to drink
text: Give small sips of an oral rehydration solution, which you can buy without a prescription, according to MedlinePlus [3]. The SEUP recommends waiting 20 minutes after a vomit, then giving 2–5 ml of oral rehydration solution every 5 minutes for an hour, and increasing the frequency if he keeps it down [5]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks [5]. Keep offering his normal food in smaller, more frequent amounts, and avoid fatty foods, sweets and juices [2]. See a doctor if he vomits a lot, cannot keep down solids or liquids, or vomits green, bloody or coffee-ground material [2].

q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
The main risk of vomiting is dehydration, according to the SEUP [1]. Signs to watch for are a child who is drowsy or listless, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears, or passes little urine [7]. If you notice any of these, or if your child vomits a lot and cannot keep down solids or liquids, they should be seen [7].

To help prevent it, offer oral rehydration solution: after a vomit, wait 20 minutes, then give 2–5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour, and increase slowly if it is well tolerated [4]. Avoid homemade solutions and fizzy drinks [4].

q: my 5 year old has been coughing all night, what can I do
text:
A cough that keeps a child awake at night is often a sign of the bronchi narrowing, and in preschool children the most frequent trigger is a viral cold [1]. The SEUP describes these episodes as cough, breathlessness and a whistling sound when breathing out, sometimes starting after a cold or exercise [5]. If your child has been diagnosed with asthma, inhaled medicines such as salbutamol relieve this narrowing, and inhalers must always be given with a spacer, never straight into the mouth [1][7].

See a doctor urgently if your child is very restless or drowsy, turns blue or pale, breathes faster and faster, or needs inhalations every two hours or less [7].

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text:
A cough lasting about a week after a cold is common, and some symptoms of a cold can last 10 to 14 days, according to MedlinePlus [6]. If the cough is barking and sounds like a seal, or comes with a hoarse voice or noisy breathing, that points to croup, according to the NHS [2]. A cough that comes in bouts and is worse at night, sometimes with a "whoop" or vomiting after coughing, suggests whooping cough, according to the NHS [4].

See a doctor if your child is struggling to breathe, has blue, grey or pale skin, lips or tongue, is sleepier than normal or difficult to wake, or is unusually quiet and still [7].

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text: A cough without fever, with normal eating, is not one of the warning signs the NHS lists for a child who needs urgent help [1]. A high temperature in children is the body's natural response to fighting infections like coughs and colds [1]. Keep offering fluids and let them rest; a poor appetite for a few days is not harmful [3]. See your doctor if your child does not want to eat, is not their usual self and you are worried, or has a high temperature lasting 5 days or more [1].

q: my daughter has red spots all over her stomach and they appeared today
text:
Red spots that appear suddenly can have several causes, and the pattern matters more than the colour. Raised, itchy patches or spots could be hives, which can usually be treated at home, according to the NHS [5]. Chickenpox spots can be anywhere on the body, including inside the mouth, and may be red, pink or darker than the surrounding skin [4]. Measles also causes a red, blotchy rash, often with fever, cough, runny nose and conjunctivitis, according to MedlinePlus [2].

See a doctor if your daughter has swelling around her mouth or is struggling to breathe [5].

q: my 2 year old has little red bumps on his legs and keeps scratching them
text: Itchy red bumps on the legs in a small child can be scabies, which causes severe itching that is often worse at night, along with bumps and itchy lines on the fingers, wrists, arms, legs and belt area, according to the WHO [5]. In infants and small children the rash can be larger, including on the palms, soles, ankles and scalp [5]. Scratching can let bacteria into the skin and cause impetigo, so it is worth having your child seen. Eczema is another common cause of dry, itchy skin in children, and scratching makes it redder and itchier, according to MedlinePlus [1]. See your doctor so the rash can be looked at and treated properly.

q: these spots dont seem to bother her but there are more every morning
text: Spots that don't bother her and keep appearing each morning are common in nappy rash, according to the NHS: red or raw patches on the bottom or nappy area, sometimes with spots, pimples or blisters, and the skin may look scaly and dry [1][2]. q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Most head injuries in children are not serious, according to the NHS [2]. After a blow to the head, the usual symptoms are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness, according to the SEUP [1].

Watch him over the next 24 hours for warning signs, and get urgent medical help if any appear [2][5]:

- He was knocked out, cannot stay awake, or has a seizure [2]
- Repeated vomiting, worsening headache, confusion, or trouble speaking or walking [4]
- Clear fluid or blood from the nose or ears, or bruising behind the ears [2][4]

He can sleep, but after a more significant knock it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6]. Rest from sport and screens for 24 to 48 hours, then return gradually to normal activity [4]. If you are worried about any symptom, have him seen [5].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text: At around 6 months, milk still gives your baby most of their energy and nutrients while they get used to eating, according to the NHS [2]. Start with small amounts and increase them gradually as your baby grows, and offer foods one at a time so you can spot any allergic reaction, such as a rash, diarrhoea or vomiting [1][3]. Keep breastfeeding or formula feeding alongside the food [2][3]. There are foods to avoid for now: no honey and no cow's milk before 12 months, and no unpasteurised drinks or foods [1]. Also avoid choking hazards like sweets, popcorn, whole nuts and whole grapes until age 3 [1]. Ask your baby's pediatrician if you have questions, especially about peanut products or if your baby was born prematurely [1][2].

q: how much water can a 9 month old drink
text: For a 9-month-old, breast milk or formula stays the main drink, and the AEP recommends keeping it on demand, without reducing the number of feeds [2]. Water is not needed in large amounts at this age: the AEP notes that babies need very little salt because their kidneys are still immature, and the same caution applies to how much they drink beyond milk [2]. Offer water in a cup with meals, but let your baby decide how much — the AEP says the caregiver offers healthy food and drink and the baby decides the amount [6]. If your baby is unwell, the WHO advises increasing fluids, including more frequent breastfeeding [1]. Ask your doctor if you are worried about how much your baby is drinking.

q: my baby refuses vegetables but eats fruit all day
text: A baby refusing vegetables while eating fruit all day is common, and the AEP advises offering the whole variety of fruits and vegetables progressively, at any daily meal, varying how they are presented — puréed, mashed or in small pieces [2]. There are no better fruits than others to start with; it depends on the family's tastes [2]. Taste for different flavours, including bitter ones like some vegetables, is shaped early, and early exposure to different flavours may reduce the risk of refusing new foods [2]. Fruit juice offers no nutritional benefit over whole fruit and can displace other foods, so whole fruit is recommended [2]. Keep offering vegetables without forcing, alongside the fruit.

q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text: At 13 months, formula should be a complement to food, not the main source of nutrition: complementary feeding means offering solid or liquid foods other than breast milk or infant formula as a complement, not as a replacement for it, according to the AEP [2]. From 6 months onwards, nutritionally adequate and safe complementary foods should be introduced while milk feeding continues [1]. The WHO recommends breastfeeding continue up to 2 years or beyond alongside those foods [1], and the first two years are especially important because optimal nutrition during this period reduces illness and supports growth and development [3]. If you are concerned about how much she is eating or her growth, speak to your doctor.

q: how often should a newborn poop
text: It is not essential for a baby to pass a stool every day: the rhythm and consistency of stools varies from one person to another, according to the SEUP [3]. What matters more than the number is the consistency — constipation is when stools become excessively hard, with discomfort or incomplete passing, and it may come with fewer stools than usual [6]. In a baby under 6 months, keep the usual feeding with breast milk or formula [3]. See your doctor if there is blood in the stool, a lot of abdominal pain, or repeated vomiting with no tolerance of solids or liquids [3].

q: my 9 month old suddenly wakes up every two hours at night
text: Waking every two hours at night is common at this age: night wakings are physiological, and around 30% of children still wake at night by their first birthday, according to the PUC Chile manual [1]. Each sleep cycle lasts about 90 minutes, so brief wakings between cycles are expected [1]. If your baby always falls asleep in your arms, they will look for that same condition to fall back asleep, so the manual suggests letting them settle themselves rather than intervening, to avoid creating a sleep habit [1]. Insomnia in infants is most often due to habits rather than illness [4]. If your baby seems unwell, is feeding poorly, or the waking comes with fever or breathing problems, see your doctor.

q: my 4 year old wakes up coughing only when he lies down
text:
A cough that comes on at night or early in the morning is one of the symptoms of asthma in children, according to MedlinePlus [4]. Other signs include chest tightness, shortness of breath or rapid breathing, wheezing (a whistling sound when breathing out), feeling tired, and trouble eating [4]. These symptoms can be mild or severe, and may happen often or only once in a while [4].

See a doctor if the coughing is severe, if he has serious breathing problems, or if he turns very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [4].

q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text: Using a reliever inhaler more often than usual is one of the signs that needs medical review: the SEUP says to seek urgent care if inhalations are needed very frequently, every two hours or less [6]. Salbutamol opens the airways and relieves symptoms, and most mild attacks can be managed at home with it [2][3]. It should always be given through a spacer, never straight into the mouth, because it works less well that way [6]. Watch for breathing that gets faster, ribs or chest pulling in, or a bluish colour around the lips — these mean it is getting worse [5][6]. If there is no clear improvement, the child needs to be seen at a health centre [6].

q: my baby has a temperature of 100.4, is that considered a fever
text:
100.4 °F = 38 °C.

If your baby is under 3 months old, a temperature of 100.4 °F needs a doctor the same day.

For an older baby, yes — 100.4 °F (38 °C (100.4 °F)) is considered a fever, according to the NHS [1][3]. A normal temperature in babies and children is about 36.4 °C (97.5 °F), and a high temperature is usually 38 °C (100.4 °F) or above [3]. Fever is not a disease; it is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Most fevers in young children settle within 1 to 4 days [1]. You can usually care for them at home with plenty of fluids and food if they want it, checking on them regularly, including at night [2]. Get medical advice if you are worried, or if they are under 3 months with a temperature of 38 °C (100.4 °F) or higher [5].

q: my child has a fever but his hands are freezing cold
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Cold hands and feet in a child with fever: it may be poor circulation, get it checked
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

Cold hands and feet can be part of how the body responds to fever: the temperature control centre raises the body's set point, and the body responds with narrowing of the blood vessels in the arms and legs and with shivering, according to the SEUP [7]. Fever itself is a normal and healthy response to infection, and it does not mean the illness is more serious [5]. What matters is how your child looks and behaves, not the number on the thermometer alone [5].

Give plenty of fluids, do not bundle them in too many clothes or bedclothes, and do not sponge them down to cool them [2][6]. If they are uncomfortable with a temperature above 38°C (100.4 °F), you can give the antipyretic your paediatrician usually recommends; the dose depends on their age and weight [6]. Do not give aspirin to a child under 16 [2].

See a doctor if your child is drowsy, hard to wake, breathing fast or with difficulty, not drinking, or has a rash that does not fade when pressed [1][2].

q: my baby has a temperature of 105 F, what should I do
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Fever above 40.5 °C (105 °F)
text:
105 °F = 40.6 °C.

If your baby is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

For an older child, a fever is the body's way of fighting an infection, and most are caused by common viral illnesses, according to MedlinePlus [2]. Give plenty of fluids, keep breastfeeding if you are breastfeeding, and offer food if they want it [3]. You can give paracetamol or ibuprofen if they are distressed or uncomfortable, checking the packaging or leaflet for the right dose for their age and weight [3]. Fever usually lasts two to four days, and it often does not come all the way down after medicine — that alone does not mean things are worse [5]. Watch their general condition and colour, and check for red spots that do not fade when you press them [5]. Get medical advice if you are worried, or if the medicine is not helping [3].

q: my child says he feels like he cant catch his breath but his oxygen monitor says 99
text:
A normal oxygen reading does not rule out breathing trouble: the SEUP says to watch for difficulty breathing — ribs pulling in, the chest sinking, fast breathing, or getting tired when walking or running — and to go to the emergency department when breathing difficulty appears [1]. Trust what you see in your child, not only the monitor: if he is working hard to breathe, struggling to speak, or looking worse, get him seen now.

q: my 3 year old has had a fever since yesterday but is drinking and peeing
text: Fever with drinking and peeing normally is reassuring, but a fever in a 3-year-old can be a sign of a urinary tract infection, according to the NHS [6]. Children with UTIs may have a high temperature, appear generally unwell, be irritable, not feed or drink properly, wet the bed or themselves, or be sick [6]. Other signs include pain or burning when peeing, needing to pee more often, cloudy or bloody pee, and pain in the lower tummy or back [1]. If you think your child may have a UTI, it is important to see your doctor, who can check with a urine test; treatment is with antibiotics [3]. See your doctor if the fever is very high or low, if your child seems unwell, or if symptoms get worse or do not improve within 48 hours [7].

q: my baby has red cheeks but no fever
text: Red cheeks on their own are not a sign of anything serious, and a flushed face can simply mean your baby is warm. A normal temperature in babies is around 97.5°F (36.4°C (97.5 °F)), and a fever is usually considered to be 100.4°F (38°C (100.4 °F)) or above, according to the NHS [2]. Babies with a high temperature may feel hotter than usual on their back or chest, feel sweaty or clammy, and have flushed cheeks [2]. If you think your baby has a high temperature, check it with a thermometer so you can work out whether you need medical advice [2]. Spots on a baby's cheeks, forehead and chin appearing up to 6 weeks after birth could be baby acne, which needs no treatment and usually gets better after a few weeks or months [5]. See your doctor if your baby feels hot to touch, is feeding less than usual, or seems drowsy or unwell.

q: my son is 4 and weighs 25 pounds, is that too little

q: my 2 year old weighs 40 pounds, should I be worried
text:
40 lb = 18.1 kg.

I can't tell from a weight alone whether your 2-year-old is in a healthy range — that depends on their height and their growth curve over time, not on one number. The WHO defines overweight in children under 5 as a weight-for-height more than two standard deviations above the median of its growth standards, and obesity as more than three [4]. It also notes that for young children the aim is to avoid restrictive diets while they are still growing [1]. If you're concerned, your doctor can plot their weight and height on the growth chart and tell you how they're tracking.

Note: 18.1 kg is very high for a child of 2 years on the WHO growth charts. If it was a typo, correct it, because doses go by weight; if it is right, mention it to your doctor.

q: my child tested positive for COVID and has a fever
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day. For an older child, a high temperature is very common and usually returns to normal within 1 to 4 days, according to the NHS [2]. Fever is a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most causes are mild viral infections [3]. Treat the discomfort, not the number: keep your child well hydrated, in a comfortably cool room, and avoid overbundling [5]. Paracetamol or ibuprofen can help, at the dose your pediatrician recommends, but they do not cure the infection and the fever may come back when they wear off [5]. Do not give aspirin to a child under 16 [7].

See a doctor if the fever lasts 5 days or more, your child is not eating or not acting like themselves, or shows signs of dehydration such as fewer wet diapers, sunken eyes, or no tears when crying [7].

q: my son had croup last winter and now has a barking cough again
text:
A barking cough that comes on suddenly at night, after a few days of cold-like symptoms, is typical of croup, according to the SEUP [3]. Croup is an inflammation of the vocal cords and windpipe, usually caused by a virus, and it is often worse at night [1]. Most cases are mild and get better on their own in a few days, though the cough can last up to a week [4][1]. Offer fluids if there is a fever and use the usual fever medicine [4].

See a doctor if your child is struggling to breathe, has blue, grey or pale skin, lips or tongue, is sleepier than normal or difficult to wake, or is drooling and finding it hard to swallow [7].

q: what should I know about malaria symptoms in a child returning from Africa
text:
The first symptoms of malaria are usually fever, headache and chills, and they typically appear 10 to 15 days after the bite of an infected mosquito, according to the WHO [2]. Because these early symptoms look like many other febrile illnesses, it is worth getting a test as soon as possible [2]. Infants, children under 5, travellers and pregnant women are at higher risk of severe infection [2].

Severe malaria can include extreme tiredness, confusion, seizures, difficulty breathing, dark or bloody urine, yellowing of the eyes and skin, or abnormal bleeding — these need emergency care quickly [2].

Anyone with symptoms after travelling to an area where malaria is common should see a doctor promptly [2].

q: mi hijo tiene fiebre despues de las vacunas
text:
Si el bebé tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico ese mismo día.

En un niño mayor, la fiebre después de las vacunas es una reacción esperable y suele ser pasajera. La inmunogenicidad y la seguridad de las vacunas sistemáticas son, en general, similares a las de otros niños, y no hay motivo para retrasar la vacunación si no existe una contraindicación clara [3][5]. La dosis de antitérmico depende de la edad y el peso, así que consúltala con su pediatra o con el prospecto.

Consulta a tu médico si la fiebre es alta o dura más de lo esperado, o si el niño está decaído, irritable o con mal aspecto.

q: my 18 month old has a fever of 103 and won't take Tylenol
text:
103 °F = 39.4 °C.

A fever is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most children get better within 1 to 4 days, according to the NHS [5]. The main goal at home is your child's comfort, not bringing the number down by itself [3]. Keep offering plenty of fluids, dress them lightly and don't over-wrap them [3]. If they won't take Tylenol, you can try ibuprofen instead, as long as they are over 6 months old — but never give aspirin to a child [4]. Both paracetamol and ibuprofen work about the same and are given at the dose your doctor recommends, every 6 to 8 hours [3]. See a doctor if the fever lasts more than a few days, or sooner if your child seems very unwell, is not drinking, or has a seizure [5].

q: can I give him both Tylenol and Motrin at the same time
text: No, do not give them at the same time. According to the NHS, you should not give ibuprofen and paracetamol together, but you can alternate between them if a doctor or nurse tells you to [2]. If you do alternate, write down when you gave each medicine so the doses stay evenly spaced and your child does not get too much [2]. Ibuprofen can be given 3 to 4 times in 24 hours, depending on your child's age and dose [2]. Check the packet or leaflet for the correct dose [2].

q: why does my 3 year old have a temperature of 105 degree celsius
text:
105 °F = 40.6 °C.

A temperature of 105 °C is not possible — that reading is almost certainly Fahrenheit, and 105 °F is about 40.5 °C (104.9 °F), according to the AEPap [6]. Fever is not an illness: it is the body's normal response to an infection, and most fevers are harmless and settle on their own [6]. It rarely goes above 40.5 °C (104.9 °F) [6]. Most fevers are caused by infections, and the treatment depends on the cause, according to MedlinePlus [2].

See a doctor if your child is very drowsy, has trouble breathing, a stiff neck, a rash that does not fade when pressed, or a seizure.

q: my 5 year old won't stop itching her arms and legs at night
text: Itching that is worse at night is a classic sign of scabies, an itchy rash caused by mites that spreads through close skin contact and should be treated quickly to stop it spreading, according to the NHS [5]. The itch of scabies is often severe and worse at night, with itchy lines and bumps on the fingers, wrists, arms and legs, according to the WHO [2]. Many other things can also cause itchy skin and rashes in children, so it is worth having your child checked [5]. See your doctor so the cause can be confirmed and treated properly.

q: can my 10 year old take adult Tylenol if I cut it in half
text: No, do not cut an adult Tylenol in half for a 10-year-old. Acetaminophen (Tylenol) helps reduce fever in children and adults, and you should know how much your child weighs before giving it, according to MedlinePlus [1]. The right amount depends on the child's weight, so check the children's product or ask your doctor or pharmacist. Paracetamol is a common painkiller for children that relieves pain and high temperature, according to the NHS [5]. Speak to a pharmacist or doctor if you're not sure [3].

q: my 14 year old says her throat hurts really bad when swallowing
text:
A sore throat that hurts when swallowing is a common symptom, and tonsillitis is one possible cause: the tonsils at the sides of the throat become red and swollen, and swallowing can be painful [2]. Sore throats are usually caused by viruses like a cold or flu, and only occasionally by bacteria [4]. For relief, she can drink plenty of water, eat cool or soft foods, suck ice cubes or hard sweets, and rest [5].

See a doctor if the sore throat does not improve after a week, or sooner if she has a very high temperature, signs of dehydration, or difficulty breathing or swallowing [7].

A fever is a sign your body is fighting an infection, and chills often come with it — most infections that cause fever are mild, usually viral [3]. Fever usually lasts two to four days, though it can last longer without being more serious [4]. Most fevers are caused by infections, as the body tries to kill the virus or bacteria behind them [1].

See a doctor if the fever lasts five days or more, or if you feel very unwell, confused, drowsy, or have difficulty breathing [7].

q: he has an inhaler but I dont know when to use it
text:
A spacer helps the medicine reach the lungs better, and inhalers should always be used with one, never straight into the mouth, according to the SEUP [1]. For a child with wheezing, treatment with salbutamol is started, and if there is no clear improvement you should go to a health centre [1]. Use it when the child has cough, trouble breathing or whistling sounds from the chest, which are the signs of an asthma attack [2][3]. If inhalations are needed very often — every two hours or less — that is a reason to seek care [1].

See a doctor if the child is very restless or drowsy, turns blue or pale, breathes faster and faster, or the chest and ribs pull in when breathing [1].

q: my daughter touched a hot pan and has a red patch on her finger
text: A red patch after touching a hot pan is a burn, and cooling it under running water for 15 to 20 minutes is the first thing to do, according to the Niño Jesús hospital guide [3]. Remove any rings or tight clothing from the finger straight away, cover the area with a clean cloth, and do not put ointment on it or burst any blisters [3]. You can give paracetamol or ibuprofen for the pain [3]. See a doctor if the burn affects the hands, so a burn on a finger should be checked [3].

q: my 9 month old still has no teeth, is that normal
text: It is normal for a first tooth to appear later than 8 months; the usual range is between 4 and 8 months, according to MedlinePlus [4]. Even before any teeth come through, wipe your baby's gums with a damp washcloth after each meal [4]. Once the first tooth shows, switch to a soft toothbrush [4]. Do not put your baby to bed with a bottle of milk, juice or sugar water — use only water for bedtime bottles [4]. Ask your health care provider whether your baby needs oral fluoride [4].

q: my child has chickenpox, when can he go back to school
text:
Children usually miss 5 to 6 days of school or childcare because of chickenpox, according to the CDC [1]. A child with chickenpox can pass it on until all the spots have crusted over, so they should stay away from school until then [2]. Chickenpox illness usually lasts about 4 to 7 days [1].

See your doctor if your child seems very unwell, has trouble breathing, or the skin looks infected.

q: she bumped her forehead on the table and cried right away, do I need to watch her
text: Yes, she should be watched for the first 24 hours after the blow, according to the SEUP [4]. Most head injuries in children are mild and not dangerous, and most recover quickly [4][5]. Watch for a headache that is intense, getting worse, or not relieved by paracetamol or ibuprofen, repeated vomiting, confusion or drowsiness, or, in a very small child, being irritable or hard to wake [2]. Also watch for blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears, or trouble speaking or walking [2]. See a doctor if any of these appear, or if her behaviour worries you [7].

q: I read that vaccines can cause autism, is that actually true
text: No, that is not true. Many scientific studies have looked at this and found no link between vaccines and autism, according to MedlinePlus [2]. Vaccines are safe and must go through extensive safety testing before they are approved in the United States [2]. Children get their vaccines at well-child visits, following the schedule published by the CDC [4].

q: my daughter has a seizure right now, what do I do

text: Keep your daughter safe while you wait for medical help. Check the time the seizure starts and ends, protect her head with your hands or something soft, and remove any dangerous objects nearby, according to the NHS [5]. Lay her on her side in a safe place and do not put anything in her mouth, according to the SEUP [6]. If the seizure has stopped, put her in the recovery position [6]. After a first febrile seizure, she needs to be checked by a doctor [4][6].

q: my toddler has very hard poop and cries when he goes
text:
Hard poop that hurts to pass is constipation, and it is common and usually not serious [3]. Constipation means the stool is hard and dry and sometimes painful to pass, according to MedlinePlus [3]. The main thing is to offer more liquids, preferably water, and more foods with fibre — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables [1]. Don't replace fruit with juice, because juice has little fibre [1]. It usually gets better by changing the diet, and sometimes with a laxative if a paediatrician prescribes one [1].

q: my baby has been vomiting for six hours but still wants to breastfeed
text:
Keep breastfeeding — offer it normally, and even more often if your baby wants it, according to the SEUP [1]. Give smaller amounts more frequently to reduce the risk of vomiting, and don't force food [3]. Avoid fizzy drinks and sugary juices, which can make vomiting worse [3][5]. Vomiting usually settles on its own within less than a week [3].

See a doctor if your baby vomits a lot and can't keep down solids or liquids, vomits even without taking anything, or if the vomit is green, bloody or looks like coffee grounds [4]. Also seek care if they are drowsy, floppy, very thirsty, have sunken eyes, cry without tears or pass little urine [4].

q: my 6 year old has a cough that is worse at night
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common in several childhood illnesses, and the organisations describe what to look for. In croup, a barking cough that sounds like a seal, a hoarse voice and a rasping sound when breathing in are often worse at night, according to the NHS [3]. A cough that comes in bouts and is worse at night can also be whooping cough, which may bring a "whoop" sound between coughs and can last several weeks [4]. Asthma can cause a persistent cough, especially at night, along with wheezing or chest tightness [5].

See your doctor if your child is getting worse, is struggling to breathe, or you are worried about their breathing [3][6].

q: my child keeps scratching red patches on his arms
text: Itchy red patches on the arms are often eczema, which is not contagious and is common in babies and children [1]. text:
Vomiting after a head injury is one of the signs that needs to be checked in the emergency department, according to the SEUP [1]. The medical team will do the examinations they consider necessary and decide whether any extra tests are needed, although in most cases these are not necessary [1].

While you are on the way, keep your son with you and do not give him anything to eat or drink unless a doctor tells you to [1]. If he becomes drowsy, floppy, or is hard to wake, tell the staff as soon as you arrive [2].

q: my daughter has mosquito bites all over her legs, what can I put
text:
Mosquito bites usually itch, and most insect bites are not usually serious and get better in a few days, according to MedlinePlus [1][2]. To stop the itch getting worse, do not let her scratch the bites, as scratching can make them infected [7]. A pharmacist can suggest treatments such as antihistamines and steroid creams for the itch [7].

See a doctor if the skin around a bite feels hot or looks red, is painful or swollen, or has pus or fluid coming out, or if she has a high temperature with swollen glands [7].

q: my 3 year old is coughing mostly at night, should I use a nebulizer
text: A night-time cough in a 3-year-old can have several causes, and the organisations describe them rather than a nebulizer. A cough that is worse at night can be part of whooping cough, which starts like a cold and then brings coughing bouts that are worse at night, according to the NHS [2]. Asthma also causes coughing that is worse at night or early in the morning, according to MedlinePlus [4]. Croup causes a barking, seal-like cough and is often worse at night, according to the NHS [3]. None of these say to use a nebulizer at home; that is a treatment your doctor decides on. See your doctor if the cough is getting worse or is not getting better [7].

q: my son has been vomiting since morning and cannot keep ORS down
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomits everything and keeps nothing down: it is a danger sign — get seen today
text:
A child who keeps being sick and cannot keep fluid down needs to be seen today [2][3]. While you wait, offer oral rehydration solution in small, frequent sips rather than a full glass at once, and keep breastfeeding or formula feeding as usual if your son is on milk [7]. Do not water down formula, and avoid fruit juice, fizzy drinks and sports drinks, which can make vomiting worse [5][7].

See a doctor urgently if the vomit is green, contains blood or looks like coffee grounds, or if your son is drowsy, floppy, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears or is passing little urine [4][5].

text: बच्चे का वज़न कितना है? पैरासिटामोल की खुराक उम्र से नहीं, वज़न से तय होती है: वज़न बताइए, फिर सही मात्रा बताई जाएगी।

missing: वज़न के बिना भी सुरक्षित अनुमानित खुराक (जैसे 15 mg/kg प्रति खुराक, हर 4-6 घंटे, अधिकतम 4 खुराक/दिन)

डॉक्टर से तुरंत मिलने के संकेत: 3 महीने से कम उम्र, सुस्ती, दौरा, सांस लेने में तकलीफ, 3 दिन से ज़्यादा बुखार, पानी की कमी

q: मेरे बच्चे को कल से दस्त हो रहे हैं और वह खाना नहीं खा रहा
banner: 💛 यह ज़रूरी है और आप अकेले नहीं हैं। Tele-MANAS 14416 पर कॉल करें (या 112 पर अगर खतरा अभी है)। अगर बच्चे ने खुद को नुकसान पहुँचाया है, तो अभी इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: खानपान के विकार के संकेत
text:
दस्त में बच्चे को खाना खिलाना बंद नहीं करना चाहिए — डब्ल्यूएचओ के अनुसार पोषक तत्वों से भरपूर खाना, जिसमें मां का दूध भी शामिल है, दस्त के दौरान भी जारी रखना चाहिए [2]। इलाज में ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्ट (ORS) का घोल और ज़िंक की खुराक दोनों शामिल हैं; ज़िंक दस्त की अवधि लगभग 25% तक कम करता है [2]। SEUP के मुताबिक उपवास ज़रूरी नहीं है — बच्चा लगभग सामान्य खाना खाता रहे, बस थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और बार-बार, उसकी भूख का सम्मान करते हुए [6]। चिकनी चीज़ें, मिठाई और जूस से बचें; दही-दूध जैसे डेयरी उत्पाद ज़रूरी नहीं कि हटाएं, और स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक न दें [6]।

अगर बच्चा बहुत उल्टी करे, तरल भी न रख पाए, या उल्टी हरी, खून वाली या कॉफी जैसी भूरी हो, तो डॉक्टर से मिलें [6]। खून वाले दस्त, लंबे समय तक चलने वाले दस्त या निर्जलीकरण के संकेतों में भी स्वास्थ्यकर्मी से सलाह लें [2]।
sources: [2] WHO — "Diarrhoeal disease", section "Prevention and treatment", p. 1 — https://www.who
[6] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿DEBEMOS OFRE

missing: निर्जलीकरण के चेतावनी संकेत: पेशाब कम/8 घंटे से नहीं, मुँह सूखा, आँसू नहीं, सुस्ती
ORS कैसे और कितनी मात्रा में दें (हर दस्त के बाद उम्र के हिसाब से)
ज़िंक की खुराक कितने दिन और कितनी मात्रा में
दस्त के साथ बुखार/खून हो तो तुरंत डॉक्टर के पास जाना
util.note: चेतावनी स्तर मानसिक स्वास्थ्य/खानपान विकार का है जबकि बच्चे को दस्त और निर्जलीकरण का खतरा है; निर्जलीकरण के संकेत और ORS की मात्रा नहीं बताई गई।

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दाने कई बीमारियों में हो सकते हैं। हैंड, फुट एंड माउथ डिज़ीज़ में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने का मन न करना होता है, और कुछ दिन बाद मुँह के छाले तथा हाथ-पैरों पर उभरे हुए लाल दाने निकलते हैं, जो फफोले बन सकते हैं — यह NHS के अनुसार है [3]। यह आमतौर पर 7 से 10 दिन में खुद ठीक हो जाता है और इसका कोई दवा से इलाज नहीं है [1]। खसरे में दाने पहले लक्षणों के 3 से 5 दिन बाद चेहरे पर बालों की लाइन से शुरू होकर नीचे की ओर फैलते हैं, और दाने निकलते समय बुखार तेज़ हो सकता है — यह CDC के अनुसार है [4]। चिकनपॉक्स में खुजली वाले दाने शरीर पर कहीं भी हो सकते हैं, और उससे पहले या बाद में तेज़ बुखार और बेचैनी हो सकती है [5]।

दवा की खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए वह डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार ही दें। अगर दाने के साथ मुँह के आसपास सूजन हो या बच्चे को साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो, तो तुरंत मदद लें [6]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

[3] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Symptoms of hand, foot and mout
[4] CDC — "Measles Symptoms and Complications", section "3–5 days after symptoms begin: me
[5] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Symptoms of chickenpox", p. 1 —
[6] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Raised, itchy spots or patches"

missing: कौन से खतरे के संकेत हैं जिनमें तुरंत डॉक्टर के पास जाना चाहिए (जैसे बच्चा सुस्त/जगाने पर न जागे, पानी न पी पाए, गर्दन अकड़, तेज़ साँस, दाने दबाने पर गायब न हों)
बुखार उतारने के लिए पैरासिटामोल की उम्र/वज़न के अनुसार खुराक और बुखार नापने का तरीका
घर पर क्या करें: तरल पदार्थ/ORS छोटे-छोटे घूँट में, हल्के कपड़े, आराम, खुजली में क्या करें
भारत में कब और कहाँ दिखाएँ (नज़दीकी डॉक्टर/आपातकालीन नंबर) तथा दाने वाले बच्चे को स्कूल/दूसरे बच्चों से दूर रखना

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
नहीं, यह हल्के में लेने वाली बात नहीं है — कम पेशाब और कम दूध पीना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है, और ऐसे में तुरंत डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है [1]।

तब तक, SEUP के अनुसार, बच्चे को भूखा न रखें — स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से, और अगर बच्चा माँगे तो उससे भी ज़्यादा बार कराते रहें [1]। मुँह से दिया जाने वाला ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन घोल (ORS) थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में, बार-बार दें, ताकि उल्टी का जोखिम कम हो [1]। खेल-कूद वाले पेय (स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक) और जूस न दें, क्योंकि उनमें शक्कर बहुत ज़्यादा और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट का संतुलन बच्चे के लिए अनुपयुक्त होता है [1]।

अगर बच्चा बहुत उल्टी करे, तरल भी न रख पाए, या उल्टी हरी, खून वाली या कॉफ़ी जैसी भूरी हो, तो तुरंत आपातकालीन विभाग जाएँ [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿DEBEMOS OFRE

missing: 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए ORS की मात्रा/बारंबारता (जैसे हर 1-2 मिनट में 5-10 ml चम्मच से)
निर्जलीकरण के अन्य चेतावनी संकेत: आँखें धँसी, आँसू न आना, सूखा मुँह, 6-8 घंटे से पेशाब न आना, सुस्ती
पेशाब कम होने का मतलब स्पष्ट करना (जैसे 6-8 घंटे में गीला डायपर न होना)
भारत में कहाँ जाएँ/किसे मिलें (नज़दीकी अस्पताल/आपातकालीन नंबर) और घर पर निगरानी कैसे करें
util.note: सही आपातकालीन सलाह है, पर ORS की मात्रा और निर्जलीकरण के चेतावनी संकेत स्पष्ट नहीं हैं।

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी होने पर डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है। SEUP के अनुसार अगर बच्चा तीन महीने से छोटा है, या गिरावट एक मीटर से ज़्यादा ऊँचाई से हुई है, तो भी तुरंत डॉक्टर के पास जाना चाहिए [1]। डॉक्टर ज़रूरी जाँच करेंगे और देखेंगे कि आगे कोई टेस्ट चाहिए या नहीं, हालाँकि ज़्यादातर मामलों में इसकी ज़रूरत नहीं पड़ती [1]।

रास्ते में बच्चे को होश में रखने की कोशिश करें और उल्टी होने पर उसे करवट पर लिटाएँ ताकि कुछ भी साँस की नली में न जाए। अगर बच्चा सुस्त लगे, बेहोश हो जाए, बार-बार उल्टी करे, या उसका व्यवहार चिंता की बात लगे, तो तुरंत आपातकालीन सेवा से संपर्क करें [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Traumatismo craneal. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS

missing: सिर की चोट के बाद 24-48 घंटे निगरानी रखने की सलाह
खतरे के संकेत: बार-बार उल्टी, बेहोशी, दौरा, पुतलियों का असमान होना, नाक/कान से खून या पानी आना
भारत में आपातकालीन नंबर (108/112) या नजदीकी अस्पताल जाने का स्पष्ट निर्देश
बच्चे को दर्द की दवा (जैसे इबुप्रोफेन) बिना डॉक्टर की सलाह के न देना
util.note: La respuesta se basa en una guía española (SEUP) y no menciona el número de emergencia ni el sistema sanitario de India, aunque la situación requiere atención urgente.

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
कब्ज़ के कारण बच्चा पॉटी करते समय रो सकता है — रोने के आम कारणों में कब्ज़ भी शामिल है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [2]। अगर बच्चा लगातार रो रहा है और आप उसे चुप नहीं करा पा रहे, या रोना उसके सामान्य रोने जैसा नहीं लग रहा, तो यह बीमारी का संकेत हो सकता है [4]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर बच्चा रोते-रोते पीला पड़ जाए, पसीना आए, सुस्त लगे या दूध पीना छोड़ दे, या उसे बुखार हो, उल्टी हो या पॉटी में खून आए [6]।
sources: [2] NHS — "Colic" (2022), section "Symptoms of colic", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/condition
[4] NHS — "Soothing a crying baby" (2026), section "Crying and illness", p. 1 — https://ww
[6] SEUP — "Cólico del lactante. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS

missing: पॉटी नरम करने के लिए फाइबर/पानी/जूस जैसे घरेलू उपाय
शिशु की उम्र के अनुसार इलाज (जैसे 6 महीने से कम उम्र में सिर्फ डॉक्टर की सलाह)
कब्ज़ के लक्षण: कड़ी/सूखी पॉटी, दिनों तक पॉटी न आना, पेट में दर्द
गुदा में दरार या ब्लीडिंग होने पर क्या करें
util.note: जवाब कब्ज़ के इलाज और घरेलू उपायों के बारे में कुछ नहीं बताता, सिर्फ रोने और डॉक्टर से मिलने की बात करता है।

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
बुखार चढ़ते समय बच्चे का ठंड लगना और हाथ-पैर ठंडे होना सामान्य है, ऐसा SEUP कहता है [1]। बुखार उतरते समय बच्चा पसीना-पसीना और गर्म हो जाता है [1]। बुखार आमतौर पर 2 से 4 दिन रहता है [2]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर बच्चा सुस्त या बहुत चिड़चिड़ा लगे, साँस लेने में तकलीफ हो, त्वचा पर ऐसे लाल धब्बे हों जो दबाने पर गायब न हों, या वह कुछ भी खा-पी न पाए [7]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁLES SON LOS SÍNTOMAS?",
[2] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁL ES LA EVOLUCIÓN ESPERA

missing: बच्चे की उम्र के हिसाब से बुखार नापने और तापमान बताने का तरीका (जैसे 38°C/100.4°F से ऊपर)
बुखार के लिए पैरासिटामोल/आइबुप्रोफेन की सही खुराक और अंतराल
पानी/ORS छोटे-छोटे घूँट में पिलाना और पर्याप्त पेशाब की निगरानी
3 महीने से छोटे बच्चे में बुखार हो तो तुरंत डॉक्टर के पास जाना
util.note: हाथ-पैर ठंडे होने की व्याख्या ठीक है, पर बुखार नापने, दवा की खुराक और तरल/पेशाब की निगरानी जैसी व्यावहारिक बातें नहीं बताई गईं।

q: मेरा बच्चा बहुत सुस्त है और ठीक से जाग नहीं रहा
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: जवाब नहीं दे रहा; बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text: बच्चे का सुस्त हो जाना और ज़्यादा देर जागते न रहना गंभीरता के संकेत हैं, विकासपीडिया के अनुसार — ऐसे लक्षण दिखते ही तुरंत चिकित्सकीय सहायता लेनी चाहिए [2]। साँस लेते समय पसलियों का अंदर खिंचना, सीने से कराहने जैसी आवाज़, या त्वचा, होंठ, नाखून और चेहरे पर नीली झलक भी खतरे के लक्षण हैं [2]। अस्पताल जाते समय बच्चे को खाना-पीना चालू रखने की कोशिश करें और बुखार हो तो गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं [2]।
sources: [2] Vikaspedia — "बच्चों को होने वाली आम बीमारियॉं — स्रोत: भारत स्वास्थ्य" (2020), sectio

missing: 112 पर कॉल करने या तुरंत अस्पताल ले जाने का स्पष्ट निर्देश

बच्चे को कुछ खिलाने-पिलाने से पहले चिकित्सकीय मूल्यांकन की सलाह
निर्जलीकरण के संकेत: पेशाब न आना, मुँह सूखा, आँसू न आना

util.note: आपात स्थिति बताई गई है पर 112 पर कॉल करने का स्पष्ट निर्देश नहीं दिया और बेहोशी जैसे बच्चे को खाना-पीना देने की सलाह खतरनाक है।

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text: बहुत कम पेशाब आना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है, और ऐसे में बच्चे को तुरंत देखा जाना चाहिए। तब तक बच्चे को बार-बार थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) देना जारी रखें, क्योंकि SEUP के अनुसार दस्त या उल्टी में शरीर से निकले तरल और नमक की भरपाई के लिए यही सबसे उपयुक्त है [1]। बच्चे को भूखा न रखें — SEUP कहता है कि सामान्य खाना जारी रखा जा सकता है, बस थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और बार-बार, ताकि उल्टी का खतरा कम हो [1]। मीठे पेय, जूस और स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक से बचें, क्योंकि इनमें शर्करा ज़्यादा और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट्स बच्चे के लिए अनुपयुक्त होते हैं [1]। स्तनपान कराने वाली माँ बच्चे की मांग पर पहले से भी ज़्यादा बार स्तनपान करा सकती हैं [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿DEBEMOS OFRE

missing: कितनी कम पेशाब चिंता की बात है (जैसे 8 घंटे से ज़्यादा पेशाब न आना, गीले डायपर की संख्या)
निर्जलीकरण के अन्य लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, आँसू न आना, सूखा मुँह, सुस्ती
ORS कैसे और कितनी मात्रा में दें (छोटे-छोटे चम्मच/घूँट, हर उल्टी/दस्त के बाद)
इमरजेंसी में कहाँ जाएँ / किसे बुलाएँ (भारत में 108 या नज़दीकी अस्पताल)
util.note: सलाह सही दिशा में है पर यह स्पष्ट नहीं कि कितना कम पेशाब खतरनाक है और भारत में कहाँ/किसे तुरंत दिखाएँ।

q: मेरी बेटी को तेज बुखार और बैंगनी जैसे दाग हो गए हैं
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: दबाने पर न मिटने वाले दाने (सेप्सिस या मेनिन्जाइटिस का शक)
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसे उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

तेज़ बुखार के साथ त्वचा पर ऐसे दाग जो दबाने पर भी न मिटें, तो तुरंत अस्पताल ले जाना चाहिए — यह SEUP के अनुसार आपातकालीन विभाग में जाने का संकेत है [1]। NHS के अनुसार बुखार शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक प्रतिक्रिया है, और यह आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में सामान्य हो जाता है [3]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें, और ठंडा करने के लिए उसे न निर्वस्त्र करें न स्पंज करें [2]। 16 साल से कम उम्र के बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए वह डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार ही दें [2]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS CONSULTAR EN
[2] NHS — "High temperature (fever) in children" (2025), section "Don’t", p. 1 — https://w
[3] NHS — "High temperature (fever) in children" (2025), section "High temperature (fever)

अस्पताल पहुँचने तक क्या करें: बच्चे को होश में रखें, कुछ खिलाएँ-पिलाएँ नहीं, दौरे पड़ने पर क्या करें
अन्य खतरे के संकेत: सुस्ती/जगाने पर न जागना, तेज़ साँस, ठंडे हाथ-पैर, पेशाब कम आना, गर्दन अकड़न
बुखार नापने और बच्चे की उम्र के हिसाब से पैरासिटामोल की सही खुराक
util.note: आपातकालीन बैनर सही है, पर जवाब में बैंगनी दानों का मतलब और तुरंत 112/इमरजेंसी जाने की स्पष्ट सलाह नहीं दी गई।

q: mere 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, paracetamol kitna du
text: Paracetamol bukhar aur dard mein madad karta hai, aur ise har 4 se 6 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai [3]. Aapke 3 saal ke bachche ke liye sahi matra bachche ke vajan par nirbhar karti hai, umar par nahi [3]. Isliye packet ya leaflet par likhi matra dekhein, ya apne doctor se poochhein [3]. Din mein paanch se zyada matra na dein [3].
sources: [3] AEPap — "Antitérmicos (para la fiebre)", section "¿Cuándo utilizar los antitérmicos?",

advice to use weight-based dosing and not exceed 4 doses in 24 hours
when to seek medical help (e.g. fever >3 days, lethargy, rash, dehydration)
util.note: No da la dosis concreta en mg/kg ni el máximo diario, solo dice que se mire el prospecto.

q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text: Raat ko khansi aam taur par sardi-zukam ya asthma jaisi s्थितियों mein hoti hai. MedlinePlus ke mutabiq, sardi-zukam mein khansi ho sakti hai aur yeh aam taur par ek-do hafte mein khud theek ho jata hai [1]. SEUP ke mutabiq, asthma mein khansi khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi hoti hai [3]. Agar bachche ko saans lene mein takleef, tez saans, ya hothon ke aas-paas neela rang dikhe, to turant doctor se milna chahiye [3][5].

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Aapke bete ke pairon par lal dane aur khujli heat rash (prickly heat) ke lakshan ho sakte hain — chhote, ubhre hue dane aur khujli wali feeling iske aam lakshan hain, NHS ke mutabik [6]. Heat rash aam taur par kuch dinon mein khud theek ho jata hai [6]. Ise thanda rakhna sabse zaroori hai: dheele cotton kapde pehnaayein, halki rajai use karein, aur thande paani se nahiyein [6]. Khujli kam karne ke liye thandi cheez (geela kapda ya ice pack, towel mein lipta hua) 20 minute tak lagayein, aur khujlane ke bajaye dane ko thap-thap karein [6]. Perfume wale shower gel ya cream use na karein [6].

Doctor se milein agar dane badh rahe hain, ya aapko yakeen nahi ki ye heat rash hai [6].
sources: [6] NHS — "Heat rash (prickly heat)" (2024), section "Heat rash (prickly heat)", p. 1 — ht

missing: other common causes of itchy red spots on feet in children (hand-foot-mouth disease, scabies, fungal infection, insect bites, contact dermatitis)
warning signs needing urgent care: fever, spreading rash, pus, swelling, pain, child unwell
when to see a doctor if rash persists beyond a few days or keeps coming back
avoid scratching and keep nails short; keep skin dry and cool
util.note: Solo cubre el sarpullido por calor y omite otras causas frecuentes de manchas rojas con picor en los pies y las señales de alarma.

q: mera bachcha bed se gir gaya aur ek baar ulti ki
text:
Ek baar ulti hona aur bed se girna alag-alag baatein hain, aur sources inhe alag-alag dekhte hain. Vomiting aksar 1 ya 2 din mein ruk jaati hai, NHS ke mutabiq [1]. Agar bachche ko ulti ho rahi hai, to usse paani ya ORS thoda-thoda kar ke dete rahiye, aur doodh ya formula apni normal strength par hi dijiye [1]. Bachche ko ulti rokne ki dawa na dijiye agar woh 12 saal se chhota hai [1].

Doctor se turant milein agar:
- bachcha 12 mahine se chhota hai aur aap chintit hain [5]
- bachche mein dehydration ke lakshan hain, jaise kam peshaab ya kam geele nappies [5]
- ulti 2 din se zyada chal rahi hai [5]
- ulti mein khoon ho ya ulti ka rang hara ho [5]
sources: [1] NHS — "Diarrhoea and vomiting" (2023), section "Don’t", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/symp
[5] NHS — "Diarrhoea and vomiting" (2023), section "A pharmacist can help with diarrhoea a

advice to seek urgent medical review after a head injury with any vomiting, especially in an infant
how to observe the child in the next 24-48 hours and when to wake/check them
age of the child and how the fall happened (height, surface) not asked
util.note: La respuesta trata la vomitación pero ignora que fue tras una caída de la cama: no menciona señales de alarma de traumatismo craneal ni cuándo buscar atención urgente.

q: mere bacche ko kabz hai aur potty karte waqt rota hai
text:
Kabz mein potty karte waqt bachche ka dard aur rona aam baat hai, aur yeh kabz ke lakshan hain [3]. Kabz ke liye koi dawa shuru karne se pehle apne doctor se baat karein, kyunki dose bachche ke wazan par nirbhar karta hai.

Doctor se turant milein agar bachche ko bukhar ho, doodh peena band kar de, ya 8 ghante se zyada peshab na aaye [7].

q: mere bete ko saans lene mein dikkat lag rahi hai

text:
Bachche ko saans lene mein dikkat ho rahi hai to turant medical madad lena zaroori hai — SEUP ke mutabik saans lene mein takleef, pasliyan dikhna ya seene ka dhadakna, tez saans, chalne ya daudne mein thakan, ya saans lete waqt seene mein dard, in sab par turant ilaaj ki zaroorat hoti hai [7].

Kuch bachchon mein shuruaati lakshan sardi-jukam jaise hote hain — naak behna, khaansna, halka bukhaar — aur phir saans tez ho jaati hai, doodh peene ya khaane mein dikkat hoti hai, aur ghurghur ki awaaz aati hai [5]. RSV mein bhi shuruaat halki hoti hai, lekin kuch dinon mein yeh gambhir ho sakta hai, aur bachchon mein saans lene mein dikkat iska lakshan ho sakta hai [2][4].

Agar bachcha sust ho, jagane par na jage, ya honton ya chehre ka rang neela ya grey ho jaye, to yeh gambhir sanket hain [5].

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A cough that is worse at night is a common pattern in whooping cough: after about a week of cold-like symptoms, children get coughing bouts that last a few minutes and are worse at night, according to the NHS [2]. The cough may last several weeks or months [2]. In whooping cough the coughing fits get worse and happen more often, especially at night, and can last up to 10 weeks or more, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Croup is another cause of a night-time cough — a barking cough that sounds like a seal, often worse at night, according to the NHS [5].

See a doctor if the cough is very bad and getting worse, or if your child is finding it hard to breathe properly [4].

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text: A rash that spreads over the whole body can be caused by several different illnesses, and only a doctor can tell which one it is. Measles causes a red, blotchy rash that usually starts on the head and moves down the body, along with fever, cough, runny nose and red eyes, according to MedlinePlus [2]. Chickenpox also causes a widespread, itchy rash that turns into fluid-filled blisters and then scabs, often starting on the face and chest before spreading, according to MedlinePlus [5]. Measles can lead to serious problems, and complications are more common in children under five, according to the WHO [4]. See your doctor so your child can be examined.

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
A whistling noise when breathing can be a sign of bronchiolitis, an infection of the small airways caused by a virus, most often in babies under 2 years old [4]. It usually starts like a normal cold with cough and mucus, and after 2 to 4 days breathing can become faster and feeding harder [6]. Wheezing noises are also more common with viral infections [7].

While you are on your way, keep feeding offered and watch their breathing, how well they take feeds, their colour and their temperature [5].

q: bukhar (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
6 महीने के बच्चे में बुखार बहुत आम है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में खुद उतर जाता है, एनएचएस के अनुसार [1]। 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान बुखार माना जाता है [1]। घर पर ही देखभाल की जा सकती है: खूब तरल दें, स्तनपान जारी रखें, भूख लगे तो खाना दें, और रात में भी नियमित रूप से बच्चे को देखते रहें [3]। अगर बच्चा बेचैन या परेशान लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दी जा सकती है — पैकेट या पर्ची देखकर पक्का करें कि दवा इस उम्र के लिए ठीक है, या फार्मासिस्ट या डॉक्टर से पूछें [3]। 6 महीने से कम उम्र के बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन न दें, और 16 साल से कम उम्र में एस्पिरिन न दें [2]। अगर बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा रहे, बच्चा खाना न चाहे या अपने सामान्य स्वभाव का न लगे, या पेशाब कम आए — सूखी डायपर, धँसी आँखें, रोने पर आँसू न आना — तो डॉक्टर से सलाह लें [2]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
नहीं, बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहलाना या स्पंज करना नहीं चाहिए — तेज़ तापमान शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक और स्वस्थ प्रतिक्रिया है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [7]। बुखार उतारने के लिए गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछ सकते हैं, सिर्फ माथा नहीं, और बच्चे का खान-पान चालू रखने की कोशिश करें, ऐसा भारत स्वास्थ्य बताता है [3]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें [7]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर बच्चा 3 से 6 महीने का है और तापमान 39C या ज़्यादा है, बुखार के साथ दाने हैं, बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा से है, या बच्चा खाने को तैयार नहीं है [7]।

text: 3 साल के बच्चे में सूखी खांसी और सीने से सीटी जैसी आवाज़ होना सांस की नली में रुकावट के कारण हो सकता है, जिसमें खांसी, सांस लेने में तकलीफ और सीने में "सिबिलेंस" (सीटी की आवाज़) शामिल हैं, और यह सालबुटामोल जैसी ब्रोंकोडाइलेटर दवाओं से ठीक हो सकता है [2]। प्रीस्कूल उम्र के बच्चों में सीटी की आवाज़ का सबसे आम कारण सांस की वायरल संक्रमण होता है [2]। अस्थमा में भी सांस की नलियां सूजकर सिकुड़ जाती हैं, जिससे सीटी की आवाज़, खांसी और सीने में जकड़न होती है [4]। अस्थमा के लक्षण हल्के या गंभीर हो सकते हैं और समय-समय पर आते-जाते रहते हैं; लक्षण दिखने पर स्वास्थ्यकर्मी से मिलना चाहिए [5]।

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
लाल दाने और खुजली के साथ त्वचा में सुरंग लगाने वाले छोटे कीड़े (स्केबीज़) हो सकते हैं, जिसका इलाज आमतौर पर घर पर ही किया जा सकता है [4]। स्केबीज़ एक परजीवी संक्रमण है जो त्वचा में घुसकर अंडे देता है और तेज़ खुजली व दाने पैदा करता है, और यह त्वचा से त्वचा के संपर्क से फैलता है [2]। इलाज क्रीम या मुँह से ली जाने वाली दवाओं से होता है [2]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें यदि:
- बच्चा 2 साल से छोटा हो और स्केबीज़ के लक्षण हों, या घर में किसी और को भी स्केबीज़ हो [1]
- त्वचा में संक्रमण लगने का लगे या एक्ज़िमा जैसी कोई और त्वचा की समस्या हो [1]
- फ़ार्मेसी का इलाज पूरा होने के 2 से 4 हफ़्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी रहे [1]

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text:
हाँ, एमएमआर वैक्सीन सुरक्षित है। विकासपीडिया के अनुसार लगभग सभी वैक्सीन्स के हल्के दुष्प्रभाव हो सकते हैं, लेकिन ये सभी टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं और दुष्प्रभावों का इलाज आसानी से हो जाता है [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना यह संकेत है कि वैक्सीन असर कर रही है [6]। nidirect के अनुसार टीके सुरक्षित और प्रभावी हैं तथा गंभीर बीमारियों से बचाते हैं [4]।

भारत में एमएमआर सहित टीकों की उम्र और खुराक राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती है, इसलिए अपने बच्चे के टीकाकरण की जानकारी अपने डॉक्टर से लें [4]। अगर बच्चे का कोई टीका छूट गया हो, तो डॉक्टर से मिलकर उसे पूरा करवाएँ [4]।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
Raat ki khansi bachchon mein asthma ka ek aam lakshan hai — MedlinePlus ke mutabik asthma mein khansi khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi hoti hai [5]. SEUP ke mutabik bhi asthma crisis mein bachchon ko kabhi-kabhi raat ko khansi aati hai [1]. Agar saath mein saans phoolna, seene ka dhadakna, ya seeti jaisi awaaz ho, to yeh bhi isi taraf ishara karta hai [1][5].

Doctor se turant milein agar:
- Saans lene mein bahut takleef ho, seene ki pasliyan saaf dikhne lagein, ya bachcha bahut sust ya neend mein ho [7].
- Honth ya chehra neela ya bahut peela pad jaye [5][7].
- Khansi ke saath bukhar ya saans ki takleef badhti jaye [4].

q: mera 8 month ka baby bed se gir gaya aur ro raha hai
text: Aapke 8 mahine ke baby ko bed se girne ke baad sar par chot lagi hai, aur sar ki chot ke aam lakshan hain sar dard, bhram, ulti aur neend aana, SEUP ke mutabik [1]. Ghar par pehle 24 ghante dhyan se nigrani karein, SEUP ke mutabik [3]. Agar sar dard tez ya badhta ho, baar-baar ulti ho, ya bachcha chidchida ho ya jagaana mushkil ho, to turant doctor ke paas le jaayein, SEUP ke mutabik [2]. Doctor ke batayi hui khurak mein paracetamol ya ibuprofen diya ja sakta hai, SEUP ke mutabik [6].

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche mein red rashes ke kai kaaran ho sakte hain, aur WHO ke mutabik sarna (scabies) mein tez khujli hoti hai, khaas taur par raat mein, aur ungliyon, kalaiyon, baahon, pairon aur kamar ke aas-paas dane aur lakeerein dikhti hain [1]. Chhote bachchon mein yeh rash zyada gambhir ho sakta hai, khaas taur par hatheli, talwe aur sar ki twacha par [1].

MedlinePlus ke mutabik varicela mein bhi khujli wali rash hoti hai jo pani ki chhaale ban kar phir khuski banati hai, aur aam taur par chehre, seene aur peeth se shuru hokar poore sharir par failti hai [4]. Eccema mein twacha sookhi ho jaati hai aur khujli hoti hai, aur yeh chehra, kohni ke andar aur ghutnon ke peeche zyada hota hai [5].

Agar bachche ko tez bukhar, saans lene mein takleef, ya rash ke saath susti dikhe, to apne doctor se turant milna chahiye [3].

q: kya polio ki drop dena zaroori hai
text: Polio ki drop dena zaroori hai: bachche ko polio se bachane ke liye polio vaccine lagwana zaroori hai, aur ise samay par lagwana chahiye [3]. Spain ke vaccination calendar ke mutabik polio vaccine (VPI) 2, 4 aur 11 mahine ki umar mein lagti hai, aur 6 saal ki umar par ek booster dose di jaati hai [3]. Agar bachche ko 2, 4, 6 aur 18 mahine mein chaar doses mil chuki hain, to 6 saal par polio ke bina dTpa diya jaata hai [3]. WHO ke mutabik polio vaccine doosri vaccines ke saath mila kar di jaati hai, jaise diphtheria, tetanus aur hepatitis B ke saath [6]. Agar aapke bachche ki koi dose chhoot gayi hai, to apne doctor se milein taaki pending doses poori ho sakein [3].

q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text: Diarrhoea after a trip is usually an infection of the gut, and the main treatment is to replace the water and salts lost, according to the WHO [2]. Oral rehydration salts are a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar, and zinc supplements shorten the episode and reduce stool volume [2]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [2]. Do not use homemade solutions or soft drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [1]. See a doctor if there is blood in the stool, persistent diarrhoea, or signs of dehydration such as crying without tears, little urine or sunken eyes [2][1].

q: क्या टीका लगने के बाद बुखार आना सामान्य है?
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार होने पर उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

हाँ, टीके के बाद हल्का बुखार आना सामान्य है और चिंता की बात नहीं है। डी.पी.टी. या डी.टी. का टीका लगने के कुछ घंटों बाद बच्चे को हल्का बुखार हो सकता है, और ये लक्षण आम तौर पर 2-3 दिनों में अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]। खसरे के टीके के बाद 6-7 दिनों में हल्का बुखार और शरीर पर हल्के लाल दाने हो सकते हैं, जिनके लिए इलाज की ज़रूरत नहीं होती [5]। बुखार के लिए पैरासिटामोल दी जा सकती है, पर खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए टीका लगाने वाले स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी की सलाह मानें [5]। अगर लक्षण 2-3 दिनों में ठीक न हों, या इंजेक्शन की जगह लाल, गर्म या सूज जाए, तो स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी से परामर्श करें [5]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text:
Dizziness after being in the sun can be a sign of a heat-related illness, and children are at higher risk [3]. Move your child to a cool, shaded place, take off extra clothing, apply cool wet cloths to the forehead, neck and armpits, and offer cool water in small sips, according to the SEUP [6]. Heat stroke is serious: it can raise body temperature above 41°C and cause dizziness, nausea and confusion, and needs medical help right away [3].

See a doctor urgently if the dizziness comes with confusion, trouble speaking or moving, loss of consciousness, or vomiting they cannot keep fluids down with [7].

q: solids baby ko kab se dena shuru kare
text: Solid khana (weaning) baby ko taqreeban 6 mahine ki umar se shuru karna chahiye, NHS ke mutabiq [2]. Shuru mein yeh zyada zaroori nahi ke baby kitna khata hai — ahem yeh hai ke woh khane ki aadat pade; zyada tar energy aur nutrients abhi bhi doodh se hi milte hain [2]. 6 mahine se pehle shuru karne ki bajaye intezar karna behtar hai kyunke doodh us waqt tak zaroori energy aur nutrients deta hai, aur baby ka munh, chabana aur nigalna behtar taur par kaam karne lagta hai [4]. Doodh ke saath saath alag alag qism ke khane dene se bachay ki sehatmand khane ki aadat ban sakti hai [2]. Agar baby waqt se pehle paida hua tha, to solid khana kab shuru karna hai is par apne doctor se mashwara karein [2].

q: my child has loose motions since morning what should I give
text:
Give your child an oral rehydration solution to replace the fluids and electrolytes lost, according to the WHO [1]. It is a mix of clean water, salt and sugar, and it is the most important step to avoid dehydration [1]. Keep offering nutritious food and breast milk during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks, and do not give medicine to stop the diarrhoea without asking your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [3].

See a doctor if the diarrhoea lasts more than a day in a small child, if there is any fever in an infant, if there is blood in the stools, or if you notice signs of dehydration such as fewer wet nappies, no tears when crying, or unusual sleepiness [2][3].

q: my 6 month old has started solids, can I give banana
text: Yes, banana is fine at 6 months. Soft fruit such as banana is a good finger food, cut into pieces big enough for your baby to grip with a bit sticking out, according to the NHS [6]. q: my 5 year old has stomach pain and constipation
text:
Stomach ache is a common symptom in children and most causes are mild and get better on their own, such as constipation, gas or a tummy bug, according to the SEUP [2]. Constipation often causes stomach ache and bloating, and it is likely if your child has not pooed at least 3 times in the last week, or the poo is large, dry, hard or lumpy, or they strain or feel pain when they poo [1].

For a 5 year old, the main things that help are more fluids, especially water, and more fibre from fruit, vegetables and wholegrain cereals — fruit is better than juice, which has little fibre [3]. Most cases improve with these diet changes, and laxatives only if a paediatrician prescribes them [3].

See a doctor if the pain is severe or your child is very unwell, there is blood in the poo, or they vomit repeatedly and cannot keep down food or drink [3].

q: my 3 year old has malaria fever or maybe teething, how can I tell
text:
Malaria and teething are told apart by what comes with the fever, not by the fever itself. The most common early symptoms of malaria are fever, headache and chills, according to the WHO [1]. Those first symptoms can be mild and similar to many other illnesses, which makes malaria hard to recognise [1]. Teething is not covered by these sources, so nothing here can confirm or rule it out.

See a doctor today if your child has fever with chills or headache, especially after being in a tropical area — malaria can become severe within 24 hours if untreated [1].

q: my child has been scratching small bumps on his body
text: Small, raised itchy spots that come and go are often heat rash, which is uncomfortable but usually harmless and gets better on its own after a few days, according to the NHS [4]. Heat rash can appear anywhere on the body and spread, but it cannot be passed on to other people [4]. To settle it, keep the skin cool with loose cotton clothing, lightweight bedding and cool baths, and give plenty of fluids [4]. For the itching, apply something cold such as a damp cloth for up to 20 minutes, and pat the rash instead of scratching it [4]. Avoid perfumed shower gels or creams [4]. See your doctor if the rash is bad, does not go away, or comes with other symptoms [5].

q: what food to give 6 month baby for first time
text: Around 6 months, milk alone no longer meets a baby's energy and nutrient needs, so complementary foods are needed, according to the WHO [3]. Start with small amounts and increase them gradually as your baby grows, and increase the variety and consistency of foods little by little [3]. Offer food before the usual milk feed, when your baby is not too tired and not too hungry, and let them set the pace [2]. Keep offering different foods even if they are refused at first — it can take 10 tries or more before a new food or texture is accepted [2]. Breast milk or first infant formula stays the main drink during the first year, and you can offer sips of water from an open cup with meals [2].

q: my 4 year old has severe cough and catarrh
text:
A severe cough and catarrh (a runny nose) can be the first phase of whooping cough, which usually lasts 1 to 2 weeks and looks like a cold, with fever, runny nose, red watery eyes, sneezing and a mild or occasional cough, according to the Government of Canada [4]. In the second phase, which lasts 1 to 6 weeks, the cough becomes more severe, with uncontrollable coughing fits that can make it hard to breathe and may cause vomiting afterwards [4]. In older children who have been vaccinated, the symptoms are often less severe [4].

See a doctor if your child has a very bad cough that is getting worse [7].

q: my 3 year old has watery stool and weakness
text: Watery stools with weakness in a 3-year-old can be gastroenteritis, which is usually not serious but can sometimes lead to dehydration, according to MedlinePlus [2]. The main treatment is oral rehydration salts, a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar that replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools, and zinc supplements, which shorten the diarrhoea and reduce stool volume, according to the WHO [6]. See a doctor if the diarrhoea lasts more than a day, if there is a change in the child's mental state such as irritability or lack of energy, or for signs of dehydration such as thirst, dry mouth, urinating less than usual or no wet nappies for 3 hours or more [2].

q: what can I give my 2 year old for diarrhoea
text: For diarrhoea in a 2-year-old, the WHO lists two key treatments: oral rehydration salts (ORS) and zinc supplements [1]. q: my baby fell from the bed and seems normal now

A head injury is the medical term for a blow to the head, which usually happens from a fall, an accident or during sport, according to the SEUP [1]. q: my 3 year old has severe chest congestion and flu
text:
A chest infection is an infection of the lungs or large airways, and it often follows a cold or flu, according to the NHS [2]. The main signs are a chesty cough, sometimes with green or yellow mucus, wheezing, shortness of breath, chest pain, a high temperature, headache, aching muscles and tiredness [2]. These symptoms are unpleasant but usually get better on their own in about 7 to 10 days, and the cough and mucus can last up to 3 weeks [2]. Flu itself usually starts suddenly with fever, cough, sore throat, body aches and fatigue, and most people recover within a week, according to the WHO [3]. Rest and plenty of fluids help [3].

See a doctor if your child is breathing fast or working hard to breathe, is struggling to feed or drink, or seems very unwell [5][6].

q: what solids to give first to 6 month baby
text: Introducing solid foods should start when your baby is around 6 months old, according to the NHS [3]. At the beginning, how much they eat matters less than getting used to the idea of eating — they still get most energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [3]. Give a variety of foods alongside milk, and increase the amount and variety gradually until they can eat the same foods as the family in smaller portions [3]. You can offer purées, mashed or finger foods, or a combination — there is no right or wrong way [1]. Offer sips of water from an open or free-flow cup with meals [4]. If your baby was born prematurely, ask your doctor for advice on when to start [3].

q: my 1 year old baby body is very hot since morning
text:
A fever is a body temperature higher than normal, usually around 37 °C, and it is not an illness in itself — it is a sign the body is fighting an infection, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Most often it lasts two to four days, and it can keep going after a fever medicine without that meaning things are worse, according to the SEUP [2]. Fever medicines like paracetamol or ibuprofen can lower it, but they do not always bring it all the way down [2][3].

See a doctor if your baby is limp, barely responsive or very irritable, is breathing with difficulty, has spots that do not fade when pressed, will not take any food or drink, or is under 2 months old [7].

q: my baby has vomiting and loose motion since morning
text:

q: can I give ORS to my 1 year old after diarrhea
text: Yes, you can give oral rehydration salts to your 1-year-old after diarrhoea. The WHO lists rehydration with ORS as a key treatment for diarrhoea, and says diarrhoea should be treated with ORS, a solution of clean water, sugar and salt [1][6]. The WHO also lists zinc supplements as a key treatment: they reduce how long the diarrhoea lasts by 25% and are linked to a 30% reduction in stool volume [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. See a doctor for persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, or signs of dehydration [1].

q: mi hija se ha caido de un segundo piso pero parece estar bien

text:
La caída desde una altura superior a un metro es motivo de consulta en urgencias, según la SEUP [3]. El personal médico hará las exploraciones necesarias y valorará si hacen falta pruebas adicionales [3].

Mientras tanto, los síntomas que deben vigilarse son el dolor de cabeza intenso o que no mejora, los vómitos repetidos, la desorientación o confusión, los cambios en el comportamiento, la dificultad para hablar o caminar, y la salida de sangre o líquido claro por la nariz o los oídos [6]. En niños muy pequeños, también la irritabilidad o la dificultad para despertarlos [6].

Tras el golpe se recomienda reposo físico y mental de 24 a 48 horas, sin deporte ni pantallas, y una vuelta gradual a sus actividades [6].

q: mi hijo de 15 años tiene dolor en el pecho despues de hacer deporte
text: El dolor de pecho tiene muchas causas distintas y, en la mayoría de los casos, no está causado por un problema del corazón, según el NHS [2]. Un dolor que aparece después de hacer ejercicio o de una lesión en el pecho, que empeora al respirar hondo y mejora con el reposo, puede deberse a un esguince o distensión muscular [2]. También la ansiedad o un ataque de pánico pueden provocar un dolor a menudo agudo y continuo, con latidos más rápidos, sudoración y mareos [2]. La ansiedad es una respuesta natural ante situaciones percibidas como amenazas, y sentirla de forma ocasional es normal, según la SEUP [7]. No te autodiagnostiques: si te preocupa, consulta con tu médico [2].

q: mi hija se desmayo jugando al futbol pero ahora esta bien
text:
El desmayo o síncope es una pérdida de conocimiento brusca y corta, y suele ocurrir cuando no llega suficiente sangre u oxígeno al cerebro, según la SEUP [1]. El calor, el esfuerzo, el dolor o el miedo son situaciones que lo favorecen [1]. Antes de perder el conocimiento puede haber náuseas, visión borrosa, sudoración o zumbidos, y tras un rato de reposo los niños suelen recuperarse en un par de minutos [2][5].

Conviene consultar en urgencias si el desmayo ocurrió haciendo ejercicio físico o esfuerzo, si tardó más de 3-5 minutos en recuperar el conocimiento, o si hubo palpitaciones, dolor en el pecho, sacudidas o pérdida de orina [4].

q: mi bebe esta vomitando y no consigue quedarse con ni siquiera pequeños sorbos
text:
Lo más importante es evitar la deshidratación, y para que las soluciones de rehidratación oral se toleren bien hay que ofrecerlas en dosis pequeñas y tomas frecuentes, según la SEUP [6]. Si no consigue retener líquidos, se puede intentar dar pequeños sorbos de agua o trozos de hielo para chupar, según MedlinePlus [1]. No uses soluciones caseras ni refrescos comerciales para reponer las pérdidas, y no le des medicamentos para los vómitos sin consultar con su pediatra [3].

Consulta pronto a un profesional de la salud si el bebé está irritable o con poca energía, tiene la boca seca, orina menos de lo habitual o no moja los pañales durante 3 horas o más, o llora sin lágrimas [2].

q: cuando se puede empezar con la fruta y la verdura
text: No hay una edad única: la fruta y la verdura se introducen como parte de la alimentación complementaria, y en los menores de 6 meses se mantiene la lactancia materna o la fórmula [4]. A partir de esa edad, la SEUP recomienda una alimentación variada normal, con frutas y verduras entre los alimentos que se van añadiendo poco a poco [4]. En niños mayores, las frutas y verduras son bien toleradas y forman parte de la alimentación habitual [1]. Si tu hijo está estreñido, aumentar las comidas con fibra (frutas y verduras) ayuda a ablandar las deposiciones [4]. Consulta a tu pediatra si tienes dudas sobre cómo introducirlas o si el niño está decaído o vomita repetidamente [4][5].

q: mi hija de 5 años tiene granitos rojos por la tripa que le pican mucho
text:
Los granitos rojos que pican pueden ser urticaria: su síntoma principal es un sarpullido que pica, con bultos o manchas elevadas de muchas formas y tamaños, que puede aparecer en cualquier parte del cuerpo y verse rosado o rojo [5]. En la piel morena o negra el color puede ser más difícil de ver [5].

También conviene fijarse en si los granitos no desaparecen al pasar un vaso por encima, o si hay dificultad para respirar, labios o piel azulados o pálidos, o el niño está más dormido de lo normal: en esos casos hay que buscar ayuda urgente [7].

q: mi hijo es asmatico y se le hunden las costillas al respirar
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Dificultad para respirar grave (se marcan las costillas, respira muy rápido, pausas en la respiración, color azulado)
text: El hundimiento de las costillas al respirar es un signo de dificultad respiratoria y aparece descrito en las crisis asmáticas, según la SEUP: se les marcan las costillas y las clavículas al respirar (tiraje) y respiran más rápido de lo normal [4]. En una crisis asmática, administra de 2 a 4 pulsaciones de salbutamol con cámara espaciadora, de una en una, y repite esa dosis a los 10-15 minutos [6]. Mantén al niño en reposo, evita el humo del tabaco y la contaminación, y si toma tratamiento de mantenimiento, que lo siga tomando durante la crisis [6]. Si la crisis no cede tras el tratamiento en casa, o si te queda alguna duda, acude lo antes posible a un centro sanitario y lleva la cámara espaciadora [6].

q: y si no le baja la fiebre le puedo dar dalsy
text: Sí, se puede: si el paracetamol no mejora el malestar a las 3-4 horas, es razonable dar ibuprofeno en su lugar, según la AEPap [6]. El ibuprofeno (Dalsy) es uno de los antitérmicos más usados y tiene una eficacia similar a la del paracetamol, según la SEUP [1]. No conviene alternarlos de forma sistemática cada 3-4 horas salvo que el niño tenga malestar antes de las 6 horas [1]. La dosis de ibuprofeno depende del peso, así que confirma la cantidad con tu pediatra o con el prospecto [6]. Consulta si está decaído, le cuesta respirar, tiene manchas que no desaparecen al presionar, no tolera líquidos o es menor de 2 meses [7].

q: mi hijo tiene diarrea pero quiere comer normal
text: Sí, puede seguir comiendo: no hace falta ayunar y los niños deben mantener una dieta prácticamente normal, salvo que un médico indique lo contrario, según la SEUP [7]. Conviene darle las comidas en cantidades más pequeñas y más frecuentes, respetando su apetito [7]. Es mejor evitar los alimentos muy grasos, los dulces y los zumos, y no hace falta quitar los lácteos [7]. Lo más importante es evitar la deshidratación, ofreciéndole solución de rehidratación oral en tomas pequeñas y frecuentes [3]. Consulta a tu pediatra si rechaza comer o beber, si tiene dolor abdominal persistente o intenso, o si las deposiciones son muy líquidas y frecuentes [2].
